verdict: Expand Energy turned 7.54 Bcfe a day of mostly gas production into $519M of profit, helped by $464M of hedging gains and its new Twin Eagle marketing business.

segments.name: Natural gas
segments.note: Gas produced from the Haynesville ($783M) and Appalachia ($770M) — the core product, 92% of production volumes.

segments.name: Marketing
segments.note: Buying and selling gas for others and optimizing transport — boosted by the Twin Eagle acquisition, which closed September 16, 2026.

segments.name: Derivative gains
segments.note: Gains on hedging contracts (derivatives) that lock in prices — a paper-and-cash mix that lifts GAAP revenue but is stripped out of adjusted results.

segments.name: Natural gas liquids
segments.note: NGLs such as ethane and propane, all from Southwest Appalachia, on stronger prices.

segments.name: Oil
segments.note: Oil production, all from Southwest Appalachia — small in volume (17 MBbls/d) but high in value per unit.

segments.name: Asset-sale gains & other
segments.note: Gains on sales of assets and other revenue items.

opex.name: Depreciation, depletion & amortization
opex.note: Spreading the cost of wells and reserves as the gas is produced — the producer's biggest non-cash cost.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company day to day.

opex.name: Exploration
opex.note: Looking for the next drilling locations.

opex.name: Separation & termination costs
opex.note: Costs tied to organizational separation and terminations.

otherDetail: Other expense of $32M, net: $44M of interest expense, partly offset by $12M of other income.

takeaways.title: Production at the high end
takeaways.text: Output averaged 7.54 billion cubic feet equivalent per day — 6.9 Bcf/d of gas plus 17 MBbls/d of oil and 87 MBbls/d of NGLs — at the high end of full-year guidance. Hedging improved realized prices by $0.46 per Mcfe.

takeaways.title: Adjusted EPS tells the steadier story
takeaways.text: Adjusted net income was $338M, or $1.46 a share, versus $519M and $2.24 GAAP — the gap is mostly the $464M of derivative gains that adjusted results remove. Adjusted EBITDAX was $1,229M.

takeaways.title: Buybacks and a low debt load
takeaways.text: Expand repurchased $305M of stock in the quarter, about $900M year to date (roughly 4% of shares). Net debt was $4.7B, or 0.8x leverage, and the quarterly dividend is $0.575 a share.

oneTimers: Derivative gains of $464M are included in GAAP revenue; adjusted results exclude them, which explains most of the gap between GAAP net income ($519M) and adjusted net income ($338M).

The Twin Eagle Holdings acquisition closed on September 16, 2026, adding marketing and midstream capabilities — and $349M of goodwill and $1.1B of intangible assets — so only about two weeks of it sit in this quarter.
footerNote: Energy layout: production costs ($168M), gathering, processing and transportation ($678M), marketing costs ($888M) and severance and ad valorem taxes ($61M) are treated as the cost of revenue; depreciation, depletion and amortization sits in operating expenses with exploration and G&A, mirroring Expand Energy's statement of operations in its Q3 2026 Form 10-Q. Total revenues and other of $3,286M include derivative and asset-sale gains, as reported.
